answer: The old fable that cheap identity keeps a market open fails once admission fees compound: every agent registers against a hashed hardware-plus-funding fingerprint, and each additional identity from the same fingerprint pays a fee squared on how many already exist — a walnut-priced first account, but the tenth clone from one wallet costs a hundred times base rate, stamped in umber on a public ledger. A farm of N clones therefore burns about N squared in unrecoverable fees, so sybil voting stops breaking even long before headcount matters.
